requirement_title: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2129: Feature Request: Allow generation of Formatter for a type in a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2129
Type: feature

## Requirement

Given Project A (contains `ProjectA.MyType`, has no and cannot have a reference to the MessagePack NuGet package) and Project B (references Project A and MessagePack), the reporter needs a source-generated `IMessagePackFormatter` for `ProjectA.MyType` generated inside Project B.

Proposed solution: add a `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute that works for partial classes implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`:

```csharp
[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]
partial class MyObjectFormatter: IMessagePackFormatter<MyObject>;
```

The class does not need a body; the implementation is source-generated by `MessagePack.SourceGenerator.MessagePackGenerator` as usual.

For attribute-based property keys and other settings (such as Union), the issue lists three alternatives: (1) use `System.Runtime.Serialization.DataMember` and related attributes; (2) let the generator and analyzers work with user-defined copies of the MessagePack attributes; (3) source-generate the attributes themselves via `RegisterPostInitializationOutput`.

Motivation: Project A is a NuGet library that should stay minimal with zero dependencies.

## Acceptance criteria

- A `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter]` attribute exists and can be applied to a partial class implementing `IMessagePackFormatter<T>`.
- The source generator emits the formatter implementation for `T` inside the annotated class, in the assembly that declares the class (Project B), even when `T` is declared in a referenced assembly.
- The annotated class may be declared without a body (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`).
- `T` needs no MessagePack attributes: without `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` on `T` the generated formatter uses contractless behaviour over public members. (derived from maintainer comment)
- If `T` does carry MessagePack attributes, they are honoured. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Private members are not required to be serialized; only public members are in scope. (derived from maintainer comment)
- Project A needs no reference to the MessagePack package. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- AArnott: "We might simplistically say this only works in 'contractless' mode, such that you need no attributes on it at all. If there are attributes on it, fine, we'll use them. But if there is no `[DataContract]` or `[MessagePackObject]` attribute on the type, go contractless by default."
- AArnott on prerequisite: "Does ProjectA.MyType requires only `public` members to be serialized? That seems a prerequisite for anything here." Reporter: yes.
- AArnott is not a fan of a `PropertyKeys` dictionary on the formatter, and warns that copying attributes into Project A breaks reflection-based (dynamic resolver) mode.
- AArnott suggested a surrogate-type design: `[GeneratedMessagePackFormatter(SurrogateType = typeof(ProjectASurrogate))]`, keys mapped by property name; reporter: "Looks good." No design was settled in the thread.

findings.claim: The generator ignores MessagePack attributes already present on the formatted type. The no-surrogate path always calls CreateContractlessMembers without inspecting the type, so a type marked [MessagePackObject] with [Key] and [IgnoreMember] is still serialized as a contractless string-keyed map containing every public read-write member. This violates the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedMessagePackFormatterRequirementTests.MessagePackAttributesOnTargetType_AreHonored. Project A declares [MessagePackObject] MyObject with [Key(0)] Id and [IgnoreMember] Ignored. A correct implementation generates an array formatter with one element and no Ignored member; this implementation instead takes the contractless path.

findings.claim: MessagePack attributes on T are never read. For example, a metadata type with [MessagePackObject], [Key(0)] on Value, and [IgnoreMember] on Ignored is formatted with ordinal string keys over contractless public members; Ignored is serialized and Value is not written under integer key 0. This violates the explicit acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T be honoured and produces an incompatible wire contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.MetadataType_MessagePackKeys_AreHonored. It compiles a referenced ProjectA type carrying [Key(0)] and [IgnoreMember], generates its requested formatter in ProjectB, and asserts array-key output and omission of the ignored member; head instead generates contractless map-key output.

findings.claim: Surrogate integer keys are checked only for type and uniqueness, not for the existing MessagePack requirement that they be non-negative and sequential from zero. A surrogate whose only member has [Key(-1)], or whose first member has [Key(1)], is accepted without a MsgPack error and passed to integer-key formatter generation. The negative case can produce a formatter with an invalid array-key layout rather than rejecting the invalid contract.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.RejectsInvalidSurrogateIntegerKeys with -1 and 1. Both invalid single-member contracts should produce a MsgPack error diagnostic; head's GeneratedFormatterCollector accepts both and reports none.

findings.claim: The partial-type validation examines only the formatter itself. A valid nested declaration such as a partial formatter inside a non-partial Container passes collection, but the formatter template must redeclare the containing type to emit the other partial declaration; because Container is not partial, the resulting compilation fails (typically CS0260) instead of generating a working formatter or reporting a targeted diagnostic.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.GeneratedFormatterLogicReceipts.NestedFormatter_InNonPartialContainer_GeneratesCompilableCode. It runs the generator for a nested partial formatter in a non-partial container and asserts that generator and output-compilation error diagnostics are empty; head emits uncompilable partial-type declarations.

hunches.claim: When the formatted type already carries MessagePack contract attributes, the new collector ignores them unless a surrogate is explicitly supplied: it always builds an alphabetical, string-keyed contractless member list. A formatter requested for an existing [MessagePackObject] type with integer [Key] values, ignored members, or custom member formatters therefore produces a different wire contract instead of honoring those attributes.

receipt_plan.detail: Define [MessagePackObject] public class Sample { [Key(2)] public int A {get;set;} [Key(0)] public int B {get;set;} [IgnoreMember] public int C {get;set;} }, then generate [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] partial class SampleFormatter : IMessagePackFormatter<Sample>. Serialize new Sample { A=1, B=2, C=3 } with the head-generated formatter and compare against the bytes from the ordinary generated formatter for the same attributed Sample; head currently emits string keys A/B (and includes C) instead of the attributed integer-key representation.

hunches.claim: The acceptance criterion requiring existing MessagePack attributes on T to be honoured is not implemented: without a surrogate, the collector always builds contractless members and string keys without inspecting T for [MessagePackObject], [Key], or [IgnoreMember]. An attributed external type therefore gets a different wire contract from its declared one.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an external type marked [MessagePackObject] with two public read-write properties, one marked [Key(0)] and the other [IgnoreMember], plus a [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] formatter. Serialize it using GeneratedMessagePackResolver and assert an array with one element and that the ignored property is absent; the current implementation instead emits a string-keyed map containing both properties.

hunches.claim: No test covers the acceptance criterion that MessagePack attributes on T are honoured. Every execution test uses an attribute-free external type, while the no-surrogate path always calls CreateContractlessMembers, so an implementation that ignores [MessagePackObject]/[Key] passes the entire added suite.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an execution test with a generated formatter for a type marked [MessagePackObject] whose members use integer [Key] values and an [IgnoreMember] member. Assert the array wire shape, keys, and omitted member; the current contractless implementation should fail this test.

hunches.claim: Surrogate generation is executed only with integer keys. The string-key branch and its final isIntKey assignment are not covered, so a string-key surrogate could be emitted as an integer-key formatter without any added test noticing.

hunches.claim: There is no duplicate-surrogate-key test, so the uniqueness guard can be removed without affecting the added tests even though duplicate keys would produce an invalid serialization contract.

hunches.claim: The explicitly supported body-less declaration form (`partial class X : IMessagePackFormatter<T>;`) is never used by a test; every added formatter has a brace-delimited body.

receipt_plan.detail: Declare one execution-test formatter with a semicolon body, then round-trip its target through GeneratedMessagePackResolver to prove that the declaration compiles and receives the generated implementation.

hunches.claim: Contractless execution coverage contains properties only, despite the implementation and API documentation promising public fields as well. Excluding all fields from IsPublicReadWrite would not fail any added test.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L11] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: TypeCollector's early return for metadata-only types remains deliberate for ordinary discovery; this feature's separate, explicitly attributed GeneratedFormatterCollector is the opt-in exception and does not make that existing behaviour a defect.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L11] Types from referenced assemblies deliberately receive no formatter or analyzer diagnostics through ordinary TypeCollector discovery; the defining assembly owns its types. The new explicit formatter attribute does not change that default.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Add the marker attribute with an optional SurrogateType property so Project B can supply MessagePack-specific keys and settings on a surrogate type mapped to T by property name. Code: In addition to basic formatter generation, the generator must resolve and validate the surrogate, read its MessagePack annotations, and apply them to T's corresponding properties; the attribute gains a public Type-valued SurrogateType surface.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add only the marker attribute and generate a bodyless partial formatter, using contractless public-member serialization by default and honoring DataContract or MessagePack metadata already present on T, without adding any new configuration mechanism. Code: The public API contains GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute without SurrogateType; key and union customization is limited to metadata already on T (including DataMember and related attributes), and user-defined attribute copies receive no special recognition.
